key_insight: Chiral hybrid perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$ show strong spin-split band edges from spin-orbit coupling, with NEA giving larger valence-band spin splitting and opposite spin textures for opposite handedness.
engineering_relevance: Understanding how molecular chirality and organic cation choice tune spin splitting and band structure can guide design of perovskite optoelectronic and spintronic materials with controllable circular dichroism.
method: First-principles electronic-structure calculations with spin-orbit coupling
Band-structure comparison of PEA- vs NEA-based chiral perovskites
Group-theoretical analysis of the nonsymmorphic space group $P2_12_12_1$
evidence_signal: The abstract reports calculated spin-split bands, multiband anticrossings, and symmetry-enforced degeneracies that explain why NEA has stronger effective valence-edge spin splitting than PEA.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on first-principles calculations for specific chiral perovskite structures, so real-device behavior may also depend on defects, disorder, and temperature effects.
paper_title: First-principles calculations of spin-split bands in chiral hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$
